text:
The checkout-redesign flag stayed at 5 percent for eleven days. The canary cohort was chosen by hashing user IDs into 10,000 buckets and admitting the lowest 500, and that group included too many legacy accounts created before the 2019 schema migration. Those accounts had null currency fields, and the new payment-form validation layer failed on them. This raised p99 latency from 340 to 910 milliseconds.

The dashboards showed no problem. The error budget alert threshold was averaged across all traffic, so a regression affecting one twentieth of users was hidden by the other ninety-five percent, which were healthy. Engineers assumed the ramp had stalled because of capacity. Then someone sliced the traces by cohort and found the cluster of null fields.

The fix was a two-line default, but the lesson was bigger. A ramp is a flashlight, not a floodlight: it shows only the users the hash happens to point at.
